NRC Question No. 36 - Impactive/Impulsive Loads

Question:

Questions 36.1 through 36.6 regarding LTR Section 9.0 for Evaluation of Impact and Impulsive
Loadings:

       (1) LTR Section 9.0 states, in part: "As discussed in Sections 9.1 and 9.2, these
           requirements along with the applicable modifications specified in the RG 1.243 are
           used for design basis impulsive and impactive loads for both containment and non-
           containment CSSM applications [8] ." However, the LTR does not clearly state what
           specific modifications identified in RG 1.243 are determined to be applicable to
           the LTR-proposed analysis, design, and detailing requirements of CSS structural
           elements subject to design basis impulsive and impactive loads.

            The NRC staff requests that SMR (Holtec):
               a. identify the specific modifications from RG 1.243 that are determined to be
                  applicable to the LTR-proposed analysis, design, and detailing requirements
                  of CSS structural elements subject to design basis impulsive and impactive
                  loads in accordance with Section N10.3 of ANSI/AISC N690-24, and
               b. provide the basis of the modifications in RG 1.243 related to design for
                  impulsive and impactive that are considered not applicable.
               c. Update the LTR accordingly.

       (2) LTR Section 9.1 proposes to use the approach in Section N10.3.2 "Local Response
           Evaluation" to determine the minimum required faceplate perforation thickness, tp,min
           to prevent local perforation of the rear faceplate of Concrete-Strengthened Steel
           (CSS) structural elements under design basis missile impact loads. However, being
           a design methodology, it does not state what the corresponding design faceplate
           thickness will be to prevent perforation with margin. The NRC staff requests that
           SMR (Holtec) define and provide the technical basis for, the required design
           faceplate thickness to prevent local perforation under impact from design basis
           missiles. Update the LTR accordingly.

       (3) (i) Clarify if LTR Section 9.2 "Analysis Requirements and Acceptance Criteria for
           Local Response due to Design-Basis Impulsive and Impactive Loads" is intended
           for "global or overall structural response evaluation," rather than "Local Response"
           evaluation indicated in the section title and the second sentence of the first
           paragraph of the LTR section;

            (ii) Clarify if the simplified method and refined method referred to in LTR Section 9.2
            are the methods in paragraphs N10.3.4(b) and N10.3.4(c) of AISC N690-24;

            (iii) Since no ductility limits are specified in section N10.3.4 of AISC N690-24, clarify
            if the "ductility limits" for the simplified method are intended to mean "rotation limits;"

           [g/oba~ response evaluation are based on Section N10.3.4 of AISC N690-24, which
           per detailing requirements in N10.3.3 apply to flexure-controlled failure mechanism

           Clarify LTR Section 9.2 to address the above issues and provide appropriate
           analysis requirements and acceptance criteria for shear-controlled and compression-
           controlled failure mechanisms under design-basis impact and impulsive loading.
           Update the LTR accordingly.

       (5) (i) LTR Section 9.2 provides acceptance criteria for response to CSSM structural
           elements subject to design basis impactive and impulsive loadings by reference to
           Section N10.3.4 of N690-24, which specifies rotation limit not to exceed 6 degrees
           and maximum faceplate plastic strain not to exceed 0.05 in/in. The staff notes that

NRC Question No. 45 - Containment Weld Requirements
Question:

LTR Section 11 .3.2 "Weld Examination" states: "The requirement for faceplates which form the
containment leak barrier is consistent with the weld examination of liners per Subsection CC-
5500 of ASME CC and with weld examination of metal containments per NE-5200 of ASME
BPVC Section Ill, Division 1, Subsection NE (41 )." However, LTR Table 11-5 "Weld Examination
Requirements" states in the first row that the NOE requirement is [[
                                                                     ,]] and in the third row for
n
                              ]], the NOE requirement is [[
      )). Noting that for containment pressure-resisting boundary, all CJ P welds are critical, the
NRC staff identified the following issues with the LTR weld examination requirements for
containing pressure-resisting boundary that serves containment structural integrity function and
leak-tight integrity function:
         (i) The LTR does not include the Weld Joint Categories analogous to those in
              CC-3840 (Figure CC-3831-1) and NE-3350 (Figure NE-3351-1 ) for the CSSM
              portion of containment (SCCV), including the transfer girder (TG) and interface with
              the SCV.
        (ii) For the containment CSSMs, it is not clear which weld examinations will be in
              accordance with CC-5500 and which examinations will be in accordance with
              NE-5200, or both.
       (iii) Regarding volumetric examination , it is not clear which volumetric exam ination
              method(s) (radiography, ultrasonic) will be used and for which welds.
       (iv) The LTR requirement for containment leak barrier (Containment CSSM inner
              faceplate based on audit discussion) is inconsistent with CC-5500 since it does not
              include leak testing of welds that serve the function of the containment leak barrier
              required by CC-5521(e). For CJP welds of the containment pressure-resisting
              boundary other than the leak barrier (i.e., outer faceplate which serves a structural
              integrity function), the weld examination requirements in the LTR is inconsistent with
              the applicable NE-5200 provisions, which require it to be fully (100%) radiographed,
              or when the joint detail does not permit radiography, ultrasonic examination plus
              liquid penetrant or magnetic particle examination per NE-5280.

            The NRC staff requests that SMR (Holtec) provide the following information to
            address the above issues:

            (1) Provide a Figure and corresponding weld joint categories with definitions,
                corresponding permissible types of welded joints with rules for making them ,
                and weld examination requirements for all welds of the CSSM portion of
                containment (including TG and interface with the SCV). This should be
                analogous and consistent with those in CC-3840 and NE-3350, as applicable.
                Update the LTR accordingly.
            (2) Clarify with the rationale what joint category weld examinations will be
                performed for the CSSM portion of containment (TG and below) in accordance
                with CC-5500 and related paragraphs, and what examinations in accordance
                with NE-5200 and related paragraphs . Update the LTR accordingly.
